Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Expectation2: Advocate for policy changes by contacting legislators and participating in lobbying efforts.
Situation2: A key legislative aide has just called and has ten minutes to talk right now about the bill you are campaigning for.
Story: My phone buzzes twice in quick succession. First, it’s Jamie, her voice trembling as she tells me her car has broken down on the highway, miles from home, and she’s scared. “Can you come get me? Please?” she asks, and I can hear the panic in her voice. I promise I’ll figure something out. Before I can even grab my keys, my phone rings again. It’s the legislative aide I’ve been trying to reach for weeks—he’s available for a ten-minute call right now, and this could be the moment to push our bill forward. My mind races. Jamie is counting on me to be there, to be the friend who shows up when it matters most. But the campaign team is counting on me, too; this call could make or break months of work. I feel my chest tighten as I stare at my phone, torn between the urgent needs of someone I love and the cause I’ve poured my heart into. I can’t do both. My hands shake as I try to decide which promise I have to break.
